sn11.1:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthı̄ in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park.
sn11.1:1.3: There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus thus:
sn11.1:2.1: “Bhikkhus, once in the past the asuras marched against the devas.
sn11.1:2.2: Then Sakka, lord of the devas, addressed Suvı̄ra, a young deva, thus:
sn11.1:2.3: ‘Dear Suvı̄ra, these asuras are marching against the devas.
sn11.1:2.4: Go, dear Suvı̄ra, launch a counter-march against the asuras.’
sn11.1:2.5: - ‘Yes, your lordship,’ Suvı̄ra replied, but he became negligent.
sn11.1:2.6: A second time Sakka addressed Suvı̄ra … …
sn11.1:2.9: but a second time Suvı̄ra became negligent.
sn11.1:2.10: A third time Sakka addressed Suvı̄ra …
sn11.1:2.13: but a third time Suvı̄ra became negligent.
sn11.1:2.14: Then, bhikkhus, Sakka addressed Suvı̄ra in verse:
sn11.1:3.1: “‘Where one need not toil and strive
sn11.1:3.2: Yet still may attain to bliss:
sn11.1:3.4: And take me along with you.’ [Suvı̄ra:
sn11.1:4.1: “‘That a lazy man who does not toil
sn11.1:4.3: Might still have all desires fulfilled:
sn11.1:4.4: Grant me that, Sakka, as a boon.’ [Sakka:
sn11.1:5.1: “‘Where a lazy man who does not toil
sn11.1:5.4: And take me along with you.’ [Suvı̄ra:
sn11.1:6.1: “‘The bliss, supreme deva, we might find
sn11.1:6.4: Grant me that, Sakka, as a boon.’ [Sakka:
sn11.1:7.2: Where without work one won’t decline,
sn11.1:7.5: And take me along with you.’
sn11.1:8.1: “So, bhikkhus, if Sakka, lord of the devas, subsisting on the fruit of his own merit, exercising supreme sovereignty and rulership over the Tāvatiṃsa devas, will be one who speaks in praise of initiative and energy,
sn11.1:8.2: then how much more would it be fitting here for you,609 who have gone forth in such a well-expounded Dhamma and Discipline, to toil, struggle, and strive for the attainment of the as-yet-unattained, for the achievement of the as-yet-unachieved, for the realization of the as-yet-unrealized.”
